1242 Mean, Variance, Expected Frequency of Binomial Distributions

examples.question_text: A biased coin shows heads with probability $0.35$. Let $X=1$ if it shows heads and $X=0$ otherwise. Construct the probability table and use the discrete expectation and variance formulas to find $E(X)$, $\text{Var}(X)$ and $\sigma(X)$. Give the standard deviation to three decimal places.
A machine part passes inspection with probability $0.94$. Let $X=1$ if the part fails inspection and $X=0$ otherwise. Find $E(X)$ and $\text{Var}(X)$.

methods.description: Identify the probability of the outcome coded 1, then use E(X)=p and Var(X)=p(1-p), retaining exact fractions when requested.
methods.sourceRef: booklets/mathsmap-sources/Stage 6 Extension 1/Binomial Distributions.md lines 569–599, Guided Practice a–b and Expected Value and Variance formulas

methods.description: Read or construct the probabilities at 0 and 1, calculate E(X) and E(X²) using their probability sums, then subtract [E(X)]² to obtain the variance.

examples.derivation: P(X=0)=1−0.35=0.65. E(X)=0(0.65)+1(0.35)=0.35 and E(X²)=0²(0.65)+1²(0.35)=0.35. Var(X)=0.35−0.1225=0.2275. σ(X)=√0.2275≈0.476970, giving 0.477 to three decimal places. This follows the source example at lines 547–566 with different values.
p=3/8 and 1−p=5/8. E(X)=3/8 and Var(X)=(3/8)(5/8)=15/64, both exact. The method follows the general Bernoulli formulas at lines 581–599.
The outcome coded 1 is failure, so p=1−0.94=0.06. E(X)=0.06 and Var(X)=0.06(0.94)=0.0564. Complementary success follows lines 437–467; the moment formulas follow lines 594–599.
